learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.action: Dealt one red then jumped to ten reds
Put cards back, then Keep them out

observations.outcome: Corrects prediction; explains remaining deck composition, replacement 50%, coin has no pile and no due-ness

interaction.reason: Depletion and reversible replacement directly change remaining mix and odds.

payoff.reason: Resolves wrong prediction using actual counts and replacement contrast, rejects due-ness.

clarity.reason: Legible tiles, counts and explicit controls in observed viewport; initial transient AX labels resolved visually.

transfer.reason: Coin comparison supplies concrete new case and explains condition of no depleted pile.

accessibility.reason: No systematic mode checks; initial unlabeled AX options observed but not evaluated comprehensively.

surprise.reason: Committed 50% overturned by visibly depleted red supply.

visualExplanation.reason: Empty red tiles against unchanged black tiles carry composition mechanism.

playfulness.reason: Deal and replacement toggle allow reversible comparison.

practicalValue.reason: Recognizing changing deck odds is concrete probability use.

depth.reason: Depletion, denominator change, replacement and independent coin contrast linked.

complexity.reason: Links changing numerator and denominator to probability and contrasts replacement with independence.
complexity.conceptualDemand: balanced: fractions supported by deck graphic
complexity.interfaceBurden: low: discrete deal and replacement controls

whyCool: Returning ten reds fills their empty slots and restores 50%, then keeping them out visibly returns the same deck to 38%.
caveat: The first ten red cards are deliberately imposed, not an observed random streak; coin transfer is explained rather than tested.
missingEvidence: Phone, keyboard-only, focus, contrast measurement, zoom/reflow and reduced motion untested
screenshots: Inline observed locked prediction and revealed depleted-deck state; no saved image file
